scope: SP11 Windows qcaucd SoundWire ordinary two-cycle speaker lifecycle

windows_policy.source: live Surface AUCD registry plus Surface extension INF

windows_capture.endpoint: 1 percent, unmuted during controlled marker/tail stream; restored to 1 percent muted after capture
windows_capture.dataport_programming: IDs 55-67 recur at both starts and both stops; Windows reapplies dataport hardware state rather than leaving ports active.

observed_idle_teardown: sdw_stream_remove_slave for both WSA8845 slaves on playback/VI/CPS runtimes
linux_capture.next_wake: new hw_params/add-slave/prepare/enable sequence before producer/PA wake

source_ownership.qcom_snd_sdw_startup: allocates a new sdw_stream_runtime on every ALSA startup
source_ownership.wsa884x_hw_free: calls sdw_stream_remove_slave, which frees slave port runtime and slave runtime
source_ownership.qcom_snd_sdw_shutdown: calls sdw_release_stream, which frees the sdw_stream_runtime

conclusion: Windows live tracing proves delayed 500 ms clock-stop plus start/stop dataport reprogramming. Linux additionally destroys and reallocates SoundWire topology runtime objects on every ordinary close. The next isolation should retain SP11 WSA topology objects across PA-off idle while still disabling/depreparing streams, shutting down producer/PA, and allowing bus clock-stop.
